repository_state.notes: Phase 1 Foundation complete and verified (see phase_completion_records/P001-completion.md). Phase 2 Voice in progress: jarvis_core/voice/ (engines, TTS/STT/wake-word wrappers, echo pipeline, audio I/O, permission-gated factory). 49 automated tests passing. TTS is genuinely verified end-to-end in-sandbox; STT and wake-word wrapper *logic* is verified via mocked tests, but real model download + inference + microphone capture require the owner's actual machine (this sandbox has no audio hardware and its network policy blocks huggingface.co).

implemented_features: Layered config system (defaults -> YAML file -> env overrides), validated via Pydantic (jarvis_core/config)
Structured logging to console + rotating file (jarvis_core/observability)
SQLite storage layer with permission_grants and audit_log tables (jarvis_core/storage)
Capability-based permission system: deny-by-default store, tier classification, require() enforcement gate with audit logging (jarvis_core/permissions)
Plugin manifest schema + directory-based discovery with per-plugin failure isolation (jarvis_core/plugins)
Core HTTP service (FastAPI/Uvicorn, loopback-only, enforced) with /health and /status endpoints (jarvis_core/service)
Speech-to-text via faster-whisper, lazy model loading (jarvis_core/voice/stt.py)
Wake-word detection via openWakeWord, lazy model loading (jarvis_core/voice/wakeword.py)
Real microphone/speaker I/O adapter via sounddevice (jarvis_core/voice/audio_io.py)
Echo conversation pipeline + wake-word-gated listen loop (jarvis_core/voice/pipeline.py)
verified_features: Config system: 6 automated tests passing (defaults, file override, env override, path resolution, voice config defaults/override)
Permission system: 8 automated tests passing (deny-by-default, grant/revoke, full-catalog seeding, tier mapping, require() allow/deny paths, audit-log write)
Plugin discovery/registry: 6 automated tests passing (empty dir, missing dir, valid manifest, invalid manifest isolation, no-manifest dir skipped, registry register/get/list)
Core service: 8 automated tests passing (in-process /health and /status, loopback-enforcement allow/reject cases), plus one manual real-socket smoke test
Phase 1 -- Foundation: verified complete per roadmap.md's bar. See phase_completion_records/P001-completion.md.
Text-to-speech (jarvis_core/voice/tts.py): genuinely verified end-to-end in-sandbox -- real audio files produced via the OS voice engine, 2 tests passing.

Voice wrapper logic only (NOT real model behavior): speech-to-text lazy-loading/joining logic (4 tests), wake-word lazy-loading/threshold logic (6 tests), echo pipeline + listen-loop state machine (4 tests), audio file I/O format correctness (2 tests), MICROPHONE-permission gating (3 tests) -- all against mocked model layers or hardware-free file I/O. Real transcription accuracy, real wake-word accuracy, and real microphone capture are UNVERIFIED and require the owner's actual machine.
known_risks: Primary device (HP EliteBook 645 G9) has no dedicated GPU, so the local-tier/cloud-tier split (D-0006) is a hard constraint on later phases, not a preference.
No first-party plugins exist yet, so plugin isolation has only been tested against synthetic fixtures, not a real plugin -- plugin *execution* (vs. manifest loading) is unbuilt and unreviewed.
The core service has no authentication yet; it is only safe because of the loopback-only enforcement (D-0013) -- must be revisited before any phase exposes it beyond localhost.
Android integration approach and specific cloud AI provider(s)/cost ceiling remain open, deferred to Phase 7 and Phase 3 respectively.

Phase 2 voice code has NOT been run against real microphone hardware or real wake-word/STT model inference -- this sandbox has zero audio devices and its network policy blocks huggingface.co (confirmed via 403). This is the primary blocker to marking Phase 2 verified.
next_actions: Owner runs Phase 2 on the actual EliteBook 645 G9: install deps, let openWakeWord/faster-whisper download their models over real internet, test with a real microphone and speakers.
Once confirmed working for real, write phase_completion_records/P002-completion.md documenting what was verified on real hardware, and mark roadmap.md's Phase 2 status 'verified'.
If real-world testing surfaces issues (e.g. wrong audio device, model accuracy problems), report them back for fixes before considering Phase 2 done.
After Phase 2 is verified, proceed to Phase 3 (Multi-AI Brain) so the echo pipeline can be replaced with a real response.
